thesis: Robert F. Smith argues that his transition from chemical engineering to private equity was driven by the realization that applying computing power to industrial processes eliminates waste, a principle he later applied to enterprise software by creating scalable operating procedures similar to a franchise model. He states that the founding of Vista was triggered by his observation at Goldman Sachs that investors were failing to recognize the specific impact of software as a distinct investment area, focusing instead on broader technology sectors like semiconductors.
